title: Senate Appropriators Unveil a $1.1T Pentagon Spending Bill, the US Air Force Permanently Deploys F-15EX Fighters to Kadena, and the US Army Orders Concrete Bunkers Across the Middle East
subhead: US Senate Republicans released a nearly $1.1 trillion FY2027 defense appropriations bill folding in $69 billion of reconciliation priorities as the Pentagon failed its ninth consecutive financial audit; the US Air Force deployed its first permanently assigned F-15EX Eagle II fighters to Okinawa's Kadena Air Base as South Korea scrambled jets against Russian aircraft; and the US Army ordered urgent concrete bunkers for troops across the Middle East.

sections.heading: Senate Appropriators Unveil a $1.1T Pentagon Spending Bill as the Defense Department Fails Its 9th Audit
sections.body:
Breaking Defense, The Hill, and Bloomberg — United States Senate Republicans unveiled a nearly $1.1 trillion defense appropriations bill for fiscal year 2027 on Monday, rolling roughly $69 billion in weapons procurement, shipbuilding, and missile-defense programs initially sought by the White House through budget reconciliation directly into the Pentagon's base budget (Breaking Defense, The Hill). The massive spending package arrived on the same day the Defense Department failed its ninth consecutive annual financial audit, though Pentagon Comptroller Jules Hurst asserted that a revised audit strategy puts the department on a path toward a clean audit opinion by 2028 (Breaking Defense, Bloomberg).

In Washington legal and political oversight, a federal three-judge appeals court panel heard arguments over Pentagon media restrictions requiring journalists to be accompanied by an official escort inside the building (New York Times), while incoming Democratic Representative-elect Fred Wellman of Missouri accused Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of committing war crimes during his tenure leading the department (The Hill).
sections.whyItMatters: Unveiling a $1.1 trillion defense budget on the same day the Pentagon fails its ninth consecutive audit sets up a contentious lame-duck battle over military accountability and spending caps.

sections.heading: First Permanently Assigned F-15EX Fighters Land at Okinawa's Kadena Air Base as Seoul Scrambles Jets Against Russian Aircraft
sections.body:
Defense News, The War Zone, and CNA — The US Air Force delivered its first permanently assigned F-15EX Eagle II fighters to Kadena Air Base on Okinawa, Japan, marking the first permanent overseas basing of the service's newest heavy multirole strike fighter and bringing total USAF F-15EX deliveries to 25 aircraft (Defense News, The War Zone). The deployment strengthens US tactical airpower along the First Island Chain at a time when military analysts told Defense News that China has normalized large-scale naval and coast guard flotilla operations near Japanese waters since the 2025 bilateral diplomatic spat.

Elsewhere in Northeast Asia, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff scrambled Republic of Korea Air Force fighter jets early Tuesday after multiple Russian military aircraft entered and exited the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) over the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan (CNA). Meanwhile, President Donald Trump kicked off his Asia trip with Quad consultations in Manila and suggested North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could join Thursday's Shenzhen summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin as Kim inspected North Korea's Samjiyon border zone (Reuters, The Independent, CNA).
sections.whyItMatters: Permanently stationing F-15EX fighters at Kadena restores dedicated heavy fighter capacity in Okinawa just as Chinese naval patrols and Russian air incursions test allied defenses around Japan and South Korea.

sections.heading: US Army Takes Urgent Action to Build Concrete Bunkers Across the Middle East as Iran Rules Out Nuclear Inspections
sections.body:
Defense News, The War Zone, and USNI News — The US Army issued an urgent contracting notice to construct reinforced concrete personnel bunkers at bases across Israel, Saudi Arabia, Lebanon, and the broader Middle East, acknowledging that American soldiers are 'currently at risk' while sheltering in modified shipping containers during rocket and drone attacks (Defense News, The War Zone). At sea, USNI News confirmed that the USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) Carrier Strike Group has entered the US 5th Fleet area of operations—giving US Central Command three carrier strike groups in the region as the last escorts of the USS Abraham Lincoln finally returned home—even as Vice President JD Vance insisted the Iran conflict will not become a 'forever war' (Anadolu Agency).

In Tehran, Iranian authorities announced they will bar United Nations inspectors from visiting bombed nuclear facilities until the war ends and claimed Iranian air defenses shot down an MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, where a commercial tanker also came under attack near Oman's Khasab (CBS News). Meanwhile, Yemen's government army reported 661 clashes that killed or wounded 173 Houthi fighters as government forces repositioned to defend Aden (Al Jazeera), and Syrian sources reported 23 Israeli military vehicles raided Maariya village in southern Syria (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Replacing shipping-container shelters with hardened concrete bunkers across Middle Eastern bases reflects the Pentagon's recognition that Iranian and proxy drone-and-missile threats will persist.

sections.heading: Ukraine Strikes the Kerch Bridge Twice in 24 Hours as Russian Missiles Hit Kyiv's Dnipro Bridges
sections.body:
The War Zone, France 24, and Defense News — Russia's Defense Ministry and regional authorities reported that Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Strait Bridge linking occupied Crimea to Russia for a second time in less than 24 hours following an initial overnight drone onslaught that damaged a roadway arch and backed up 2,000 vehicles (The War Zone, The Independent). Hours later, Russian forces launched a retaliatory strike against Kyiv that hit two major bridges across the Dnipro River and knocked out heating and water supplies in several districts of the Ukrainian capital (France 24, DW).

Across European defense ministries, Defense News reported that European militaries are actively hunting for homegrown software alternatives to US data-analytics contractor Palantir Technologies to reduce operational dependence on American defense firms. In European aerospace and naval programs, Italy strongly backed a rapid path for Germany to join the sixth-generation Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) fighter project (Defense News) and unveiled plans in its 2026–2028 defense planning document to develop a new naval missile launcher capable of firing MBDA's Stratus LO land-attack cruise missile (Breaking Defense).
sections.whyItMatters: Repeated Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge and Russian counterstrikes on Kyiv's Dnipro bridges demonstrate that neither side is slowing deep-strike operations ahead of Thursday's diplomatic talks.

sections.heading: New B94 Nuclear Bomb Designation Emerges as the US Navy Prepares Tomahawk Warhead Expansion and Orca UUV Deployment
sections.body:
The War Zone, USNI News, and Breaking Defense — Budget and nuclear modernization records analyzed by The War Zone revealed a mysterious new US nuclear weapon designation—the B94—the first new series designation in decades, potentially linked to an air-delivered nuclear earth-penetrating bunker buster. In conventional strike munitions, the Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division inaugurated a new 300-gallon explosive and propellant mixer that will begin producing Tomahawk cruise missile warhead components in June 2027, while Vice Adm. Oliver Lewis, a career submariner, assumed command of US 2nd Fleet in Norfolk and imagery showed a new bow sonar dome fitted to the damaged attack submarine USS Connecticut for the first time since its 2021 undersea collision (USNI News, The War Zone).

In unmanned and space systems, the US Navy expects to receive its third Orca Extra Large Unmanned Undersea Vehicle prototype soon as it prepares for operational employment (Breaking Defense), the US Marine Corps doubled and extended its contract for M27 infantry automatic rifles, and the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate expanded prototyping awards (Defense News, Breaking Defense). In orbit, space-tracking firm LeoLabs acquired FishEye to bolster missile-warning radar software even as Sunday's ULA Vulcan Centaur launch failure deepened concerns over US military space launch capacity, while the US and Russia prepared to oppose UN talks on legally binding limits for autonomous weapons (Breaking Defense, Defense News).
sections.whyItMatters: The emergence of the B94 nuclear designation, expanded Tomahawk warhead production, and the repair of USS Connecticut underscore a broad US push to reconstitute high-end deterrence stocks.

bottomLine: Tuesday's defense developments highlight a military apparatus preparing for prolonged high-intensity competition even as political leaders head to Shenzhen: Senate Republicans unveiled a $1.1 trillion Pentagon budget while the US Army rushed concrete bunkers to the Middle East and the Air Force permanently stationed F-15EX fighters on Okinawa, while back-to-back strikes on the Kerch Bridge and Kyiv's Dnipro River crossings show the Russia-Ukraine war escalating into winter.
